page: Vultr vbm-32c-755gb-amd is a bare metal server configured with an AMD EPYC 9354P processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This dedicated system features 32 physical cores and 64 virtual cores operating at a base frequency of 3.25 GHz. The hardware is equipped with 768.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 12.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided via a local 960 GB solid-state drive, and the system includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No graphics processing units are included in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance characteristics across compute and memory subsystems. The single-core CPU performance measured via stress-ng ranks in the top tier, while multi-core performance falls within the top 25 percent. Memory performance is highly competitive, with PassMark memory scores and database operations both placing in the top 10 percent. Uncached read-only memory bandwidth reaches 351.41 GB/sec, and write bandwidth is recorded at 165.96 GB/sec. For specialized workloads, the server demonstrates strong capabilities in LLM inference, achieving 55.29 tokens/sec for text generation on a medium 7B model, which ranks in the top 10 percent.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this bare metal server offers high resource density and direct hardware access without virtualization overhead. The combination of DDR5 memory bandwidth, a high-frequency AMD EPYC processor, and dedicated resources makes it highly efficient for memory-intensive and database-heavy workloads. This configuration is well-suited for hosting large-scale relational databases, executing complex data-science tasks, running memory-intensive enterprise applications, and managing high-throughput web serving or Redis deployments.
